$ node -e "if (process.argv.length > 1) console.log('copy child re-ran eval; execArgv[0]', process.execArgv[0]); else require('node:child_process').fork('./fprint.cjs', ['copy'], { execArgv: [...process.execArgv] })"   # Node v24.16.0
copy child re-ran eval; execArgv[0] -e
findings.summary: Advisory, no REV-5 artifact against the RED. The identity half of the eval-pair rule has no carrier: ADR-0449 §3 says 'any other array is taken as given', so an eval parent's copy keeps -e and rifty must name -e. An implementation that strips the eval pair from any array whenever the launch was eval passes Parity 11 (both rows []) and every ceiling row. It would still silently fork [] where Node keeps -e. A cheap fix: a fork ceiling row with an eval launch published (the worker_threads.test.ts:434 pattern) and { execArgv: [...process.execArgv] } expecting NotImplementedError('child_process.fork.execArgv') naming '-e'.

findings.summary: Precision only; rifty names this case, and no carrier depends on the wording. The entry-less fork child 'runs the program it reads from stdin' only when stdin is not a TTY, which holds for the evidence's pipe stdio. fork's default stdio inherits the parent's stdin, so from a terminal the child starts Node's REPL. Suggested wording: '(a REPL on a TTY stdin)'.
